📰 One year after the 10·11 crash, the market looks like it’s back—but a closer look at the order books shows recovery has been uneven.

More than $19 billion in leveraged positions was liquidated at the time, affecting around 1.6 million trading accounts. Open interest in perpetual futures on major platforms fell from $217 billion to $123 billion. The question now isn’t just whether prices have recovered, but whether the market can still absorb trades.

🔥 One striking contrast: spreads recovered first, while order-book depth took much longer. Independent research found that after the event, quoted spreads on some perpetual futures returned to around pre-crash levels, but top-of-book depth kept shrinking, eventually falling to just 66%–79% of its pre-crash level. Trades may look easy to execute, but that doesn’t mean there’s enough liquidity in the order book.

💡 The order books for BTC, ETH, and UNI have also taken different paths. Based on USDT-denominated depth, UNI’s 1% depth reached 120% of its pre-crash level, compared with 81.4% for BTC and 86.8% for ETH. ETH’s total depth is close to its benchmark, but buy-side depth is only 72.9% of its pre-crash level, while sell-side depth has already surpassed it. The imbalance between the two sides means looking at the total alone can be misleading.

👀 Funding conditions have improved, but it’s too soon to say everyone is back. In the third quarter of 2026, net inflows into spot BTC and ETH ETFs increased, while the relative open-interest metric for altcoins rose from an August average of 0.71 to a September average of 0.86. The data points to a shift in capital flows and risk appetite, but doesn’t prove that overall retail and institutional participation has returned to pre-crash levels.

🤔 So this recovery looks more like a gradual process: some indicators have rebounded, while buying pressure and depth have yet to catch up. When judging whether the market has recovered, do you focus more on capital flows or on actual buying demand in the order book?

translatedData.content:
Reserve Bank of New Zealand pauses digital cash development, shifts focus to modernizing payment systems

The Reserve Bank of New Zealand was once regarded as one of the world’s most transparent central banks in its approach to researching central bank digital currencies. For years, it explored options for a digital New Zealand dollar, envisaging it as a digital cash equivalent that would be a direct liability of the central bank and carry no credit risk, but it never set a clear timeline. Now, that process has been put on hold. According to a statement from a bank spokesperson, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand has paused research and development related to its digital cash proposal and shifted its focus to a broader project examining how to modernize New Zealand’s payment system. The spokesperson said that modernizing the payment system and implementing real-time retail payment options are current priorities. Although the system remains stable and reliable for most users, there is still an opportunity to make full use of its potential in the digital economy and prepare for an uncertain future. The statement also emphasized that modernized payment infrastructure would be able to support a range of emerging payment methods, explicitly including central bank digital currencies.

There are three points worth unpacking. First, a pause does not mean abandonment: by listing central bank digital currencies as one of the payment methods that future modernized infrastructure could support, the central bank signals that digital cash has been deferred as a long-term option rather than ruled out entirely. Second, the reprioritization reflects a pragmatic approach: as of 2024, only about 227,000 people in New Zealand held crypto assets, so there is little immediate retail demand for digital cash. Cryptocurrencies are treated as property for tax purposes, and local merchants have limited acceptance of crypto payments. Third, the approach is to build a scalable, modern payment infrastructure first and then make it compatible with various emerging payment methods—a strategy that puts infrastructure first.

The direct impact on crypto markets is limited. New Zealand is not a major market for crypto trading and settlement, so this news is more of a factor affecting sentiment and market narratives than a fundamental event. Indirectly, the move continues a trend among some economies of deferring retail central bank digital currencies while prioritizing payment modernization. If more small and mid-sized economies follow this approach, expectations may grow for compliant stablecoins to fill gaps in cross-border and retail payments. For major assets such as BTC, the short-term pricing implications are minimal.

From an editorial perspective, the news is unlikely to have much effect on prices in the short term. What matters more is the shift in central banks’ thinking that it reflects: the question around digital currencies is moving from whether to issue one to whether the payment infrastructure can accommodate it. If the global rollout of retail central bank digital currencies slows overall, the strategic value of payment infrastructure and compliant stablecoins may rise in relative terms. It should be noted that the latter part of this analysis is an inference based on publicly available information, and the actual timeline for implementing New Zealand’s payment modernization project remains to be seen.

content:
新西兰储备银行暂停数字现金研发 重心转向支付体系现代化

新西兰储备银行曾被视为全球对央行数字货币研究态度最透明的央行之一。多年来，该行持续探索数字新西兰元方案，设想其作为央行直接负债、零信用风险的数字现金等价物，但始终未设定明确时间表。如今，这一进程按下了暂停键。根据该行发言人声明，新西兰储备银行已暂停数字现金提案的相关研发工作，将重心转向范围更广的项目，研究新西兰支付体系现代化。发言人称，支付系统现代化与实时零售支付方案落地是当前重点工作；尽管这套系统对多数用户而言依旧稳定可靠，但仍有机会充分发挥其对数字经济的作用，为充满不确定性的未来做好准备。声明同时强调，现代化支付基础设施将能够支持各类新兴支付方式，其中明确包括央行数字货币。逻辑上有三层值得拆解。其一，暂停不等于放弃：央行把央行数字货币列为未来现代化基础设施可支持的支付方式之一，说明数字现金被后置为长期选项，而非彻底出局。其二，优先级重排反映务实取向：截至2024年，新西兰仅有约22.7万人持有加密资产，零售端对数字现金的现实需求并不迫切，而税务上加密货币被按财产处理，本地商家对加密支付接受度也有限。其三，从路径上看，先搭建可扩展的现代化支付底座、再兼容各类新兴支付方式，属于基础设施先行的思路。就加密市场影响而言，直接影响有限。新西兰并非加密交易与结算的核心市场，这则消息更多是情绪与叙事层面的变量，而非基本面事件。间接层面，此举延续了部分经济体将零售型央行数字货币后置、优先推进支付现代化的倾向；若这一思路被更多中小经济体效仿，市场对合规稳定币在跨境与零售场景补位作用的预期可能升温。对 BTC 等主流资产来说，短期定价意义不大。从编辑视角看，短期内该消息对行情影响微弱，真正值得关注的是其折射的央行思路转变：数字货币议题正从要不要发行，转向支付底座能否兼容。若零售型央行数字货币的全球节奏整体放缓，支付基础设施与合规稳定币的卡位价值或将相对上升。需要说明的是，后半部分为基于公开信息的推断，新西兰支付现代化项目的实际落地节奏仍待观察。

translatedData.title: Trading Discipline | Five Rules I Keep Beside My Screen—Sharing Them Just as They Are
translatedData.subTitle:
On emotional days, you can forget every bit of wisdom, so I wrote these rules down and stuck them up where I could see them:

One: Write down your stop-loss level before opening a position. If you can’t, don’t open one.
Two: Never risk more than 2% of your capital on a single trade. No exceptions.
Three: Never add to a losing position or average down.
Four: After three losing trades in a row, stop trading for the day. Watch, but don’t trade.
Five: Withdraw some of your profits. The money leaves, but the mindset stays.

That’s all five rules, and not one of them is about “how to read the market.” Because the reason people lose big money is never
that they misread the market—it’s that their execution goes off track. Let’s keep each other accountable.

Morning quick take: the data doesn’t lie.

In this overnight rebound, BTC climbed straight above 83313, up 2.21% in 24 hours, with a high of 84134 and $11.42 billion in trading volume. It’s just a hair’s breadth away from the daily sell level at 84511.

But the really interesting part isn’t the gain—it’s the funding rate: -0.0024%, in the negative. Price is rising while the rate is negative. In plain English: this isn’t a bubble built on a pile of leverage; shorts are paying out of pocket to keep the rally going. Shorts are sitting on unrealized losses and paying fees at the same time. That’s a better sight than any candlestick chart.

ETH is even less interested in showing off: 2503, up 3.08%, with $8.44 billion in trading volume, and a mild +0.0025% funding rate that’s almost imperceptible. No crowded trades, no overheated leverage—the rebound is moving along like a leisurely stroll.

XRP at 1.369, up 2.72%, with a funding rate of -0.0053%. BNB at 743.6, up 1.97%. It’s a broad-based rally—even the coins that were lagging earlier have caught their breath.

There are two kinds of people to worry about right now: those who panicked and handed over their coins yesterday, now staring blankly at the screen; and those only now thinking of chasing the rally, with sell pressure from people looking to break even all around 84134. Jumping in there means carrying the people who sold at a loss yesterday. The market never runs out of opportunities; what’s scarce is the discipline not to act at an emotional peak.

Direction: bulls have the upper hand. As long as BTC holds the pivot at 82748, a pullback is a level to watch. First, look for yesterday’s high at 84134 above. Only a high-volume break above the daily sell level at 84511 would truly open up more room. Below, the safeguards are yesterday’s low at 81500 and the daily buy level at 81362. If those levels break, this rebound is invalidated. When that happens, don’t get sentimental about the market—admitting you’re wrong and exiting is a virtue.

Remember: a rally with a negative funding rate is a healthy rally. The time to wake up is when the rate turns positive and spikes, and everyone starts posting screenshots of their gains. For now? Leverage hasn’t heated up yet; the market can make its own way.

After the rebound above $83K, don’t let orders eat into your profits

From last night through this morning, BTC bounced back from around $81,000 to above $83,000, while ETH and SOL also recovered. The market looks as though sentiment is returning, but what traders really need to watch isn’t the rebound itself—it’s whether execution suddenly becomes more expensive afterward.

When reviewing a trade, many people focus only on whether they got the direction right. But in an order book that’s just recovering from a sharp drop, the outcome of the same trade can often hinge on a few small details: whether the quote book has thinned out, how many levels your target order size will consume, whether the spread has widened, whether slippage is greater than it was moments ago, and whether trigger conditions have become more sensitive in a fast-moving market.

Getting the direction right is only the first step. Poor order quality can gradually erode profits through execution costs, while an inadequate risk buffer can turn volatility you could otherwise withstand into a forced position.

I’m increasingly inclined to view PerpEX as a way to compare execution: first look at the asset, then compare quote levels, depth, and estimated costs across different routes. In a rebound, don’t just ask whether you can trade—ask which route your order will take and whether you can get better execution.

content:
83K反抽后，别让订单吃掉利润

昨晚到今早，BTC 从 8.1 万美元附近拉回 8.3 万上方，ETH、SOL 也跟着修复。盘面看起来像是情绪回来了，但交易者真正要警惕的，不是那根反抽线，而是反抽之后订单环境会不会突然变贵。

很多人复盘只看“方向有没有看对”。可在这种刚从急跌里修复的盘口里，同一笔单的结果经常差在几件小事：报价层是不是薄了，目标数量会吃到第几层，价差有没有被拉开，成交偏差是不是比刚才更大，触发条件是不是在快行情里变得更敏感。

方向对，只是第一层。订单质量不好，利润会被执行成本一点点磨掉；风险缓冲不够，原本能扛的波动也会变成被动。

我现在更倾向于把 PerpEX 当成一个执行比较视角：先看资产，再看不同路径的报价层、深度和预估成本。反抽行情里，别只问能不能做，更要问这一单从哪里走，成交质量会不会更舒服。

📰 A South Korean bank is using Bitcoin as collateral for loans—but what’s the idea?

Jeonbuk Bank, a South Korean bank, has started offering Bitcoin-backed loans to business clients, with one requirement: the cryptocurrency must be held by a third party. In simple terms, businesses can use Bitcoin they own as collateral to borrow from the bank, but they don’t retain control of the Bitcoin—the third party holds it on their behalf. This is a new experiment in integrating cryptocurrency with South Korea’s real economy.

Why does this matter?
The underlying reason is that South Korea wants to integrate cryptocurrency more deeply into its economic system while avoiding regulatory risks. Banks used to be reluctant to deal with highly volatile assets like Bitcoin. Using a third-party custodian is like adding a safety measure: banks can offer the service while managing risk. It means banks are beginning to take Bitcoin’s value as an asset seriously, rather than treating it merely as a speculative instrument. In terms of regulatory trends, this is the Nth financial institution globally to try to legitimize cryptocurrency’s participation in financial activities. It’s similar to the US approving Bitcoin ETFs earlier—both moves bring virtual currencies into the traditional financial system.

Impact on the market
For BTC, this is positive news. Banks’ willingness to accept Bitcoin as collateral indirectly recognizes its status as an asset. Previously, only individuals could hold Bitcoin; now businesses can use it this way too, and more institutional money may flow into the crypto market in the future. For example, a company might pledge Bitcoin to a bank and borrow 10 billion won (equivalent to $60 million), then use the money to expand production. Bitcoin would thus go from being a virtual currency to a source of real working capital. The impact on ETH is relatively small, since ETH is already more liquid, but this also shows that banks are starting to pay attention to the crypto sector as a whole, and they may expand to ETH or other major coins in the future. As a historical reference, a project in 2018 allowed people to borrow money using Bitcoin as collateral, but a sharp price drop led to major losses for the bank. So South Korean regulators will certainly be keeping a close eye on this latest move.

Trading outlook
💡 I’m bullish on BTC in the short term, especially if its price stays above $85K. If the bank’s pilot program goes well, it could attract more businesses from South Korea and across Asia, bringing additional demand for BTC. But this outlook would no longer hold if South Korea suddenly tightens cryptocurrency regulations—for example, by requiring all collateral to be backed 100% by local currency.

📰 韩国银行用比特币做贷款抵押，到底想干啥？

韩国的一家银行 Jeonbuk Bank 开始给企业客户提供比特币抵押贷款，但有个要求：加密货币得交给第三方保管。简单说就是，企业可以用自家持有的比特币当抵押品，去银行贷款，但比特币实际控制权不在企业手里，而是由第三方代管。这对韩国加密货币怎么和现实经济结合，是个新尝试。

为什么这条新闻重要？
这件事根本原因在于韩国想让加密货币更融入经济体系，但又怕监管风险。以前银行不太敢和比特币这种波动大的资产打交道，现在用第三方保管的方式，相当于加了道保险，既能做业务，又能控制风险。这意味着银行开始认真考虑比特币的资产价值，而不只是把它当成投机品。在监管趋势上，这是全球第N个金融机构尝试让加密货币合法化地参与金融活动，和之前美国批准比特币ETF有相似之处——都是把虚拟货币往传统金融体系里塞。

对市场的影响
对BTC来说，这是利好。因为银行愿意接受比特币做抵押品，等于间接承认了比特币的资产属性。以前只有个人能持有比特币，现在企业也能这样用，未来可能有更多大钱流入加密市场。比如，一家公司把比特币抵押给银行贷了100亿韩元（相当于6000万美元），这笔钱可能就被用来扩大生产，比特币就从虚拟货币变成了实实在在的流动资金。对ETH的影响相对小一些，因为ETH本身流动性更好，但这也说明银行开始关注整个加密货币板块，可能未来会扩展到ETH或其他主流币。历史参考的话，2018年有个项目让比特币做抵押借钱，结果因为价格暴跌导致银行亏大钱，所以这次韩国银行这么干，监管层肯定盯着呢。

操作思路
💡 我觉得短期内对BTC是看涨的，尤其是当BTC价格维持在$85K以上时。因为如果银行这个试点搞得好，可能会吸引更多韩国乃至亚洲企业参与，给BTC带来额外需求。但这个判断有个失效条件：如果韩国突然加强加密货币监管，比如规定所有抵押品必须100%本币抵押，这个逻辑就作废了。

Firmus Grid 的失败不是孤例。它说明在当前熊市环境下，过度扩张、缺乏盈利能力的项目，即使拿到顶级机构融资，也可能瞬间崩盘。Maas Group 损失 699M，恰恰是投行对这类项目估值泡沫的沉没成本。这与近期 Solana 区块链崩盘、BNB Chain 交易量萎缩等事件形成呼应，显示风险投资正在进入严选期。

对市场的影响
对 BTC/ETH 的直接影响有限。但意味着：
1. 投资者会远离非核心链的投机项目，资金可能回流以太坊等成熟生态
2. 未来监管会盯紧这类投行行为，IPO 审批趋严
3. 类似 Maas Group 的机构需要加速转型，否则会持续蒸发市值

历史参考：2018 年 ICO 泡沫破裂时，大量类似 Maas Group 的孵化器集体倒闭。

操作思路
💡 BTC 如果继续守住 82K 美金，Firmus Grid 的失败反而验证了风险分散的重要性，可能推动机构投资者更青睐以太坊生态。如果跌破 80K，说明避险情绪升温，这类投行案例会引发全面抛售。**如果出现类似 Terra/Luna 的新层级崩盘，这个判断作废。**
